title: Finite scheme quotient of an admissible tame action
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$ by scheme automorphisms. Suppose $X$ has a cover by $G$-invariant affine opens and the action is tame: for every geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the order of $\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$ is invertible in its residue field. Then there is a scheme $Y$ and an invariant morphism $q:X\to Y$ which is finite surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with geometric fibres the $G$-orbits, quotient topology on $|Y|$, and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian. Every $G$-invariant morphism from $X$ to any scheme factors uniquely through $q$. For each invariant affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the cover, $q(U)$ is open, $q^{-1}q(U)=U$, and the restricted quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}(R^G)$, where $R^G=\{r\in R:g(r)=r\text{ for all }g\in G\}$. No logarithmic structure, generic freeness, integrality, excellence or finite-type base is assumed.

source.place: Exposé VI §3.2, printed p.74 (admissible underlying scheme quotient), and proof 3.7(b), printed p.75 (finite tame strict-local invariant quotient). Scheme-theoretic quotient ingredient, with tameness retained for Noetherian finiteness.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8. Supporting input: Exposé VI §3.2, printed p.74 (admissible underlying scheme quotient), and proof 3.7(b), printed p.75 (finite tame strict-local invariant quotient). Scheme-theoretic quotient ingredient, with tameness retained for Noetherian finiteness.
